Welcome to Linwood
Welcome to our website and thank you for visiting.
We hope this provides you with plenty of information about our fantastic school. If you want to ‘experience the magic’ of our school, book a visit; we would be incredibly pleased to show you around.
Linwood School is a large special school that welcomes students from a wide geographical area, supporting a comprehensive range of Special Educational Needs and Disabilities. We have several campuses and you can find out about each campus using the ‘Our School Campuses’ tab on the main menu.
For us, every child and young person truly matters, and we understand that every moment of every day counts in improving life experiences and outcomes of our students. Our bespoke curriculum and assessment pathways ensure that learning is person-centred and focus on upholding our school values of respect and harmony, inclusivity, support, responsibility, excellence, trust, and positivity. We celebrate diversity and value the contribution that every student makes. We believe everyone should have the chance to thrive, and Linwood can make this belief a reality.
We are lucky to have an exceptional team of staff. Our teachers, teaching assistants, and support teams are committed to providing the best possible opportunities for our students. We understand the importance of building relationships, motivating activities, joy, and laughter in developing engagement, promoting independence and supporting learning. We are highly aspirational for all our students.
Thank you for taking the time to visit our website and learn more about our exceptional school.
We hope to see you soon! Gemma Talbot, Executive Headteacher
Our Vision
Our vision is to create a community where everyone achieves and thrives so that all our students succeed through their education years and beyond.
Everyone is valued within a safe and nurturing environment.
All our students have full and equal access to an ambitious curriculum, rich learning experiences and high-quality personalised support.
Our Values

Then contact us today to book a visit

Business Partners
We have long-standing partnerships with Marsham Court Hotel and Tesco Extra – Bournemouth who work closely with our students to enable them to develop their employability skills and gain an overview of the hospitality industry and retail sectors.
Both offer a wealth of different work experiences such as:
Customer Service
Learn how a busy hotel cares for its guests. Understand the importance of good customer service in the retail sector.
The Restaurant/Catering
Gain hands-on experience on how a successful restaurant operates. Students have the opportunity to work within the café at Tesco.
Maintenance
Gain practical experience with the team that cares for the building.
The Kitchen
Spend time with the chefs at the heart of the hotel’s kitchen.
Gardening
Help the team keep the hotel looking its best year-round.
Housekeeping
Learn about the importance of maintaining high standards in presentation and cleanliness.
Fashion Department
Learn how to manage and display clothing stock, and security of garments.
General Merchandise
Experience how to store, present and manage stock.
Online Shopping
Learn about the importance of the internet in modern retailing and collect internet shopping for customers.
Food Stock Management
Get shop floor experience and learn about the importance of stock rotation and presentation within the food departments: dairy, fruit & vegetables, and non-perishable goods.
We work with many other businesses to support student placements, but we are always looking to expand this offer and are keen to develop relationships with new employers to support our Post 16 offer.
This can be from offering talks, workshops, work placements or experiences of the workplace. If you think you might be able to offer a student a work placement, a site visit or perhaps you would like to come and talk about your area of expertise.
Our current partners have found many benefits of being part of our Post 16 offer and are using the positive effects of being associated with such a forward-thinking approach to training young people.
If you are a business and are interested in finding out more about what we do, would like to see our project in action or discuss ways in which you could work in partnership with CHI, please get in touch.

Preparation for Adulthood & Careers at Linwood
As part of continuing education, schools must provide impartial information about future options. Here at Linwood, our Independent Advice and Guidance (IAG) Team works with students across all campuses in year 7 and above, along with their families, to help them understand their options when they leave school. This includes educational and social care options as well as work outcomes and destinations.

What is it?
A coffee morning to meet the IAG and Family Support teams and discuss future placement options.
When does it happen?
Once a term (Thursday 9.30-11.30am) – information to be sent via email and posted on school website page.
Who is it for?
For parents of Year 7 students and above.
Future Thoughts Podcasts
Further topic information about options and preparation for adulthood can be found on our Future Thoughts Podcasts featured on Linwood Radio
Future Pathways Event
Each year, usually in November, the IAG Team host a Future Pathways event, where providers from the local areas are invited to Linwood Campus to provide information about their services. Information, including dates, will be sent nearer to the event time.
Our Future Pathways Booklet provides information about further education and Post School Options for Years 10, 11 & Post-16 Students. Click on the image to download copy of the booklet.

Linwood Training, Support and Advice (LTSA)
System and Professional Leadership
LTSA offers professional development opportunities and support in the field of education. Our dedicated team is committed to offering a wide range of tailored programs that cater to the specific needs of teachers and school support staff. We prioritize the identification of top-notch teachers and leaders who excel in providing school-based professional development. Through coaching, mentoring, and evaluation, we ensure the utmost impact and effectiveness of our programs. Additionally, we offer opportunities for formal accreditation and school-based research, empowering educators to further their expertise.
BCP Council states a commitment to equity and access for all in order to ensure that every child and young person in our area reaches their full potential.
The Outreach Service forms part of BCP’s Offer for children and young people who have Special Educational Needs or Disabilities.
Three special schools in Poole; Longspee, Montacute and Winchelsea, and two Special Schools in Bournemouth; Linwood and Iford Academy, provide Outreach support for mainstream schools across the local authority area.
Our core team comprises experienced special needs teachers: between us, we have experience of successfully teaching and supporting children and young people who have a huge range of learning needs.
Our Outreach Teachers are:
To access the BCP Outreach service, please complete one of these online forms:
BCP Outreach Service
BCP Outreach whole school request
BCP Outreach individual student request
BCP Outreach Panel Dates 2026-2027
There is also a separate Occupational Therapy Outreach Service which provides guidance & support in the area of Physical Development:
schools.otsensoryoutreachteam@ bcpcouncil.gov.uk
https://bcp-school-referrals.power­appsportals.com/
Linwood Outreach is a specialist support and consultancy service offered by Linwood School. It promotes and facilitates the inclusion of children and young people with a wide range of learning needs within their school setting. We are committed to meeting the individual needs of children and young people, in a collaborative partnership with parents, other professionals, the schools and the children and young people themselves.
Our service is composed of a team of professionals including teachers and support staff who have specialist knowledge across a wide range of Special Educational Needs and Disabilities.
What are the aims of Linwood Outreach?
To find out more, download our information sheet, complete a request form or get in touch via email: ltsa@linwood.bournemouth.sch.uk
Linwood Outreach Brochure
Linwood Outreach Support Request
We recognise the important role of middle and senior leaders in supporting their peers in other schools. We can provide schools in need of support with a task force of leaders, teachers and school practitioners, experts in their respective fields and qualified to support others to improve teaching, learning and outcomes.
We can ensure that the best leaders are working to improve the quality of teaching and leadership where it is most needed.
Please contact us to discuss how we might help you and your school.
Pupil Premium review
A pupil premium review looks at how your school is spending its pupil premium funding. The purpose of the review is to improve your school’s pupil premium strategy, so that you spend the funding on approaches shown to be effective in improving the achievement of disadvantaged pupils.
https://www.gov.uk/guidance/pupil-premium-reviews
SEND review
A SEND review looks at how your education setting provides for students with special educational needs and disabilities. The review findings will help you improve your SEND provision and strategy so you can help young people achieve good outcomes.
https://www.gov.uk/guidance/commissioning-a-send-review
MAT SEND review
The MAT Review aims to support MATs in developing an understanding of effective ways to meet the requirements of all learners. For this process to have the necessary impact on learner outcomes, the MAT should have the confidence to state what it can do well and what it needs further support with. The relationship between the reviewer and the MAT must be an open, honest and collaborative one.
https://www.sendgateway.org.uk/r/matsendreview.html

Governors
The Governors are a key force in the development of Linwood School and a vital link between the school, its families and the wider community.
Governance at Linwood
School governors are one of the largest volunteer workforces in the UK, with more than 300,000 volunteers supporting schools across the country. Governors bring their time, experience and knowledge to help schools make important strategic decisions and provide the best possible education for their pupils.
At Linwood, our governing board supports and challenges the school’s leadership team to ensure our children and young people have the best possible opportunities to learn, develop and thrive.
Our governing board is made up of twelve governors: four parent governors, five co-opted governors, one local authority governor, one headteacher governor and one staff governor.
What do our Governors do?
The role of the governing board is a strategic one. The Department for Education identifies three core functions for governing boards:
At Linwood, this means governors work closely with the Executive Headteacher and senior leadership team, providing support, challenge and oversight across the school.
Governors also visit our campuses and meet with staff to develop their understanding of the school’s work and the experiences of our pupils.
What Governors don’t do
Governors are not responsible for the day-to-day running of the school. This is the responsibility of the Executive Headteacher and leadership team.
Our governing board
Our governors bring a wide range of skills, knowledge and experience, including education, finance, healthcare, technology, business and social care.
This breadth of experience is particularly valuable to Linwood as a specialist school, helping the governing board to consider the needs and experiences of our children, young people and families from a range of perspectives.
Could you be a Governor?
Being a governor is a rewarding opportunity to make a real contribution to the life and future of a school.
You do not need previous governance experience or to work in education. Training and support are available.
From time to time, vacancies arise for parent and co-opted governors. Details of current vacancies and how to apply will be published on this website.
Meetings and terms of office
The full governing board meets five times a year: twice in autumn, twice in spring and once in summer.
All Governors’ terms of office are for four years, except for the Headteacher Governor.
Contacting our Governors
Governors can be contacted by emailing Hayley Upton, Clerk to the Governors: hayleyupton@linwood.bournemouth.sch.uk
Minutes of meetings can be made available on request to the Clerk.
Co-opted Governor Vacancy

Clubs
We are delighted to be able to offer a wide range of extended services based at Linwood School and in partnership with local children and youth services.
Linwood School deliver Holiday clubs and After School Clubs as part of our contract under BCP’s Short Breaks offer. BCP subsidise holiday club places and all children who attend have an EHCP.
Each holiday period, Linwood can provide up to 60 places per week. As per contractual arrangements, we work in partnership with the local authority to allocate places.
To ensure support reaches those who need it most, priority is given to children with additional vulnerabilities, including (but not limited to) Children in Care, children supported by Children’s Social Care, and those who have recently experienced significant trauma such as bereavement, parental critical illness, or domestic violence.
Once priority places are allocated, Linwood allocates the remaining places taking a variety of factors into consideration including the need for suitably trained staff and safe groupings of children to ensure the well-being of all children attending.
While Linwood always strives to operate a fair and inclusive allocation system, consistently the demand for places far outweighs the contractual number of places we are able to offer.
